title: WEB SECURITY RECON
description: Cover your attack surface: XSS, SQL injection, CSRF, security headers, JWT weaknesses, SSRF, and the OWASP Top 10. Know how applications break before you're asked to defend them.
based_on: OWASP Top 10 (2021) & PortSwigger Web Security Academy

questions.question: Which HTTP header is used to prevent clickjacking attacks?
questions.explanation: X-Frame-Options (DENY or SAMEORIGIN) prevents the page from being embedded in an iframe, mitigating clickjacking.

questions.question: A classic SQL injection payload to bypass a login form login check is:
questions.explanation: ' OR '1'='1 turns the WHERE clause always-true, bypassing authentication. The DROP TABLE payload is destructive but doesn't bypass login.

questions.question: What type of XSS attack stores the malicious payload in the server's database?
questions.explanation: Stored (persistent) XSS saves the payload server-side and serves it to all visitors. Reflected XSS echoes the payload directly in the response.

questions.question: Which token-based mechanism is the primary defense against CSRF attacks?
questions.explanation: Anti-CSRF (synchronizer) tokens are random values tied to the user's session and validated on state-changing requests.

questions.question: Which OWASP Top 10 category covers using components with known vulnerabilities?
questions.explanation: A06:2021 covers Vulnerable and Outdated Components — using libraries, frameworks, or other software with known CVEs.

questions.question: What does the 'Secure' flag on a cookie do?

options.A: Prevents JavaScript from accessing the cookie
options.C: Restricts the cookie to HTTPS connections only
options.D: Sets the cookie's SameSite policy to Strict

questions.explanation: The Secure flag ensures the cookie is only sent over HTTPS, preventing transmission over unencrypted HTTP.

questions.question: Which HTTP method is typically used to exploit SSRF vulnerabilities to probe internal services?
questions.explanation: SSRF (Server-Side Request Forgery) typically abuses GET requests that fetch a URL the attacker controls, redirecting the server to probe internal endpoints.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of the Content-Security-Policy (CSP) header?

options.B: Mitigate XSS by controlling resource loading

questions.explanation: CSP restricts which scripts, styles, and resources can be loaded, significantly reducing the attack surface for XSS.

questions.question: In JWT, which part contains the claims (payload)?

options.D: It is encrypted and not directly readable

questions.explanation: A JWT has three parts: header.payload.signature. The second segment (payload) contains the claims, encoded in Base64URL.

questions.question: Which tool is commonly used to intercept and modify HTTP/HTTPS traffic during a pentest?
questions.explanation: Burp Suite is the de-facto web application proxy for intercepting, replaying, and fuzzing HTTP/HTTPS requests.
